ubuntu.name: Ubuntu
ubuntu.description: The most popular desktop Linux distribution. Massive community, commercial support from Canonical, and the widest software compatibility of any distro. Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' (August 27, 2026) is the current install image, with GNOME 50 on Wayland, kernel 7.0, Rust-based core utilities, and TPM-backed full-disk encryption. Supported through May 2031 (2036 with Pro).
cons: Snap packages can be slow to launch
Canonical's commercial priorities sometimes conflict with community

mint.name: Linux Mint
mint.description: The most Windows-like Linux experience. Ships Cinnamon desktop with no Snaps, excellent out-of-the-box usability, and rock-solid Ubuntu LTS base. Mint 22.3 'Zena' is current, refreshed with HWE ISOs on kernel 7.0 in August 2026. Mint 23 — Ubuntu 26.04-based, with Cinnamon on Wayland and LMDE's installer — is due December 2026.
pros: Most familiar experience for Windows users

lmde.name: LMDE
lmde.description: Linux Mint Debian Edition — the same Mint experience built directly on Debian Stable instead of Ubuntu. LMDE 7 'Gigi' (October 2025) is based on Debian 13 'Trixie' with kernel 6.12 LTS. Insurance policy for the Mint project and a great choice for Debian fans who want Cinnamon.
pros: Pure Debian base without Ubuntu layer
Same Mint tools and Cinnamon experience
Longer support cycle than Ubuntu-based Mint

fedora.name: Fedora
fedora.description: Red Hat's community distribution and the proving ground for RHEL technologies. Fedora 44 (April 28, 2026) ships GNOME 50, KDE Plasma 6.6, GCC 16, Python 3.14, and the NTSYNC kernel module for Wine and Steam; it is supported until June 2027. Fedora 45 is targeted for October 20, 2026.
pros: Latest stable software without rolling risk
cons: Short support cycle (13 months per release)
No proprietary codecs out of the box

fedora_silverblue.name: Fedora Silverblue
fedora_silverblue.description: Fedora's immutable desktop variant using OSTree. The base system is read-only with atomic updates and rollbacks. Apps are installed via Flatpak or toolbox containers. Silverblue 44 (April 28, 2026) ships GNOME 50; Fedora 45 in October 2026 brings a web-based installer to the Atomic desktops.
cons: Steeper learning curve for package management

arch.name: Arch Linux
arch.tagline: Keep it simple, build it yourself
arch.description: A rolling-release distribution with a minimal base. You build your system from scratch using pacman and the AUR — roughly 15,800 official packages and 49,000+ AUR build scripts. The Arch Wiki is the best documentation in all of Linux. The 2026.09.01 install ISO ships kernel 7.2.2 and Archinstall 4.4.

debian.name: Debian
debian.description: The grandfather of Ubuntu, Mint, and hundreds of derivatives. Famous for rock-solid stability and 69,000+ packages. Debian 13 'Trixie' (August 2025; point release 13.6 on July 11, 2026) is the active stable, with full support to August 2028 and LTS through June 2030.

opensuse.name: openSUSE
opensuse.description: Two flavors: Tumbleweed (rolling) and Leap 16.0 (October 2025), with Leap 16.1 due November 3, 2026. Leap 16 replaced the YaST installer with Agama, requires x86-64-v2, and keeps Btrfs snapshots by default. Strong enterprise heritage from SUSE, with a migration path to SLES.
pros: Modern Agama installer, shared with SUSE Enterprise
Btrfs snapshots with Snapper by default

opensuse_aeon.name: openSUSE Aeon
opensuse_aeon.description: openSUSE's immutable desktop with GNOME and Btrfs transactional updates. The base system auto-updates atomically; apps are installed via Flatpak. Aeon (GNOME) and Kalpa (KDE) variants.

popos.name: Pop!_OS
popos.description: System76's distribution built around COSMIC, a Rust-based desktop environment written from scratch. Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS ships COSMIC Epoch 1, now at Epoch 1.6 (August 2026) with per-app volume control and new Wayland protocols. Early releases drew criticism for beta-level bugs; the 1.x series has steadily closed that gap.
cons: COSMIC is younger than GNOME/KDE — fewer features and extensions
Early COSMIC releases drew criticism for beta-level bugs
Small team maintaining both a distribution and a desktop
Still on an Ubuntu 24.04 base rather than 26.04

manjaro.name: Manjaro
manjaro.description: An Arch-based distribution with a user-friendly installer, hardware detection, and a delayed package buffer for extra stability. Manjaro 26.1.1 (August 2026) brings Linux 7.2 and KDE Frameworks 6.29. Bridges the gap between beginner-friendly and rolling-release power.
pros: Arch packages without the manual setup
cons: Delayed packages can break AUR compatibility
Not pure Arch — some community friction

zorin.name: Zorin OS
zorin.description: Designed specifically for Windows and macOS migrants. Beautiful interface with switchable layouts that mimic Windows 11, macOS, or ChromeOS. Zorin OS 18.1 (April 2026) is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, adds a new Lite edition for older PCs, ships LibreOffice 26.2, and detects 240+ Windows app installers.
cons: Limited customization in free Core edition

endeavouros.name: EndeavourOS
endeavouros.description: A graphical Arch installer that stays close to vanilla Arch. 'Titan Nova' (August 2026) refreshes the ISO with KDE Plasma 6.7.4 and Linux 7.1.8 while the team finishes Triton, the upcoming Wayland-based release. The community is famously friendly and welcoming.
cons: Can still break like any Arch system

cachyos.name: CachyOS
cachyos.description: The hottest Arch derivative in 2025–2026, topping DistroWatch. Features the BORE scheduler, CPU-targeted builds (x86-64-v3/v4), AutoFDO-profiled kernels, and a Calamares installer with animated desktop previews. Recent monthly ISOs add a Hyprland/Noctalia desktop option, KDE Plasma 6.7, and Proton-CachyOS for gaming.
pros: BORE scheduler + AutoFDO-profiled kernel for top performance
cons: Custom pacman fork may cause compatibility quirks
Performance focus may not matter on older hardware

nixos.name: NixOS
nixos.description: Your entire system defined in configuration files. Atomic upgrades, instant rollbacks, and fully reproducible environments. The largest package repository (100,000+ packages in Nixpkgs). NixOS 26.05 'Yarara' (May 30, 2026) ships GNOME 50, Plasma 6.6, kernel 6.18 LTS, and systemd stage 1 by default.

tails.name: Tails
tails.description: A portable OS that routes all traffic through Tor and leaves no trace. Boots from USB, forgets everything on shutdown. Tails 7.12 (September 3, 2026) is the first release on a new two-week cadence matching Firefox, shipping Tor Browser 15.0.21. Used by journalists, activists, and privacy advocates worldwide.
pros: Amnesic — leaves no trace on disk
Portable — boots from USB on any computer
cons: Cannot persist data without extra setup

qubes.name: Qubes OS
qubes.description: Uses the Xen hypervisor to run every application in an isolated virtual machine. Qubes OS 4.3.1 (June 11, 2026) runs Xen 4.19 with a Fedora 41 dom0, Debian 13 and Whonix 18 templates, and preloaded disposables. Endorsed by Edward Snowden and the Freedom of the Press Foundation. The most security-focused desktop OS available.
pros: Isolates work, personal, and untrusted activities

whonix.name: Whonix
whonix.description: A two-VM approach to privacy: a Gateway VM routes all traffic through Tor, while a Workstation VM runs your apps. IP leaks are architecturally impossible. Whonix 18 (now stable; Whonix 17 deprecated February 6, 2026) switches to LXQt, enables IPv6 system-wide, and rewrites Kloak as Wayland-only. Runs inside VirtualBox, KVM, or Qubes.
pros: Works inside any host OS via VM
Can run inside Qubes for extra hardening

elementary.name: elementary OS
elementary.description: macOS-inspired aesthetics with the Pantheon desktop. Focuses on design, simplicity, and a curated AppCenter with pay-what-you-want apps. elementary OS 8.1.1 (February 2026) is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, makes Wayland the default session, ships kernel 6.14, and adds first-class ARM64 UEFI support.
cons: Not for power users or tinkerers

void.name: Void Linux
void.description: Fully independent distribution with its own package manager (xbps), init system (runit), and optional musl libc builds. No systemd. Fast, lean, and principled.
pros: musl libc option for minimal footprint
cons: Fewer packages than Arch or Debian
Limited documentation compared to Arch Wiki

mxlinux.name: MX Linux
mxlinux.description: A cooperative venture between antiX and MX communities. MX 25.2 'Infinity' (May 25, 2026) is built on Debian 13.5 with Xfce 4.20, kernel 6.12 LTS (or Liquorix 7.0 with Mesa 26.0 in AHS builds), Qt6-migrated MX Tools, a new text-mode installer, and dual-init (systemd or SysVinit).

antix.name: antiX
antix.description: Ultra-lightweight Debian Stable derivative for very old hardware. Can run on 256MB RAM. Uses IceWM and Fluxbox window managers. No systemd. antiX-26 'Stephen Kapos' (March 21, 2026) is based on Debian 13 'Trixie' and offers five init systems: runit (default), sysVinit, dinit, s6-rc, and s6-66.
pros: Runs on extremely old hardware (256MB RAM)

alpine.name: Alpine Linux
alpine.description: Security-oriented, lightweight distro built on musl libc and BusyBox. The de facto standard for Docker container base images. ~5MB base image. OpenRC init system. Alpine 3.24 (June 9, 2026, supported to June 2028) ships kernel 6.18 LTS, GNOME 50, KDE Plasma 6.6, COSMIC in the community repo, and Limine boot support in the installer.
cons: musl libc breaks some glibc-dependent software

gentoo.name: Gentoo
gentoo.description: Source-based distribution where you compile every package with your chosen USE flags and optimizations. Maximum control over every binary running on your system.

rocky.name: Rocky Linux
rocky.description: A 1:1 RHEL-compatible rebuild created after CentOS shifted to Stream. Rocky Linux 10.2 (May 28, 2026) tracks RHEL 10.2 with an x86-64-v3 baseline and a 10-year support lifecycle. Co-founded by CentOS co-creator Gregory Kurtzer.
cons: Not suitable for desktop daily use

alma.name: AlmaLinux
alma.description: Another RHEL-compatible rebuild, backed by CloudLinux Inc. AlmaLinux 10.2 'Lavender Lion' (May 26, 2026) stays binary-compatible with RHEL 10 while restoring x86-64-v2 hardware support and adding capabilities RHEL 10 doesn't ship. Strong cloud provider support.
pros: Wide cloud provider support (AWS, Azure, GCP)

rhel.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
rhel.description: The commercial enterprise Linux standard. RHEL 10 (May 2025, now at 10.2 from May 2026) bumps the baseline to x86-64-v3, adds the Lightspeed AI assistant, and ships kernel 6.12. 10-year support, certified hardware/software ecosystem, and professional support from Red Hat (IBM). Free for up to 16 systems via developer subscription.

bazzite.name: Bazzite
bazzite.description: An immutable Fedora Atomic-based gaming OS. Drop-in SteamOS replacement for desktops, HTPCs, and handhelds. Boots to Steam Big Picture or KDE/GNOME desktop. Build 44.20260820 (August 2026) sits on Fedora 44 with the Open Gaming Collective kernel 7.2, KDE Plasma 6.7, GNOME 50, Mesa 26.2.1, and 90-day rollbacks. Part of the Universal Blue project.
cons: Immutable model unfamiliar to traditional Linux users
Harder to customize than standard distros

nobara.name: Nobara
nobara.description: A Fedora fork by GloriousEggroll (the Proton-GE maintainer). Pre-configured with gaming tools, codecs, custom kernel optimizations, and falcond for per-game CPU tuning. KDE Plasma default. Nobara 44 (August 28, 2026) ships five editions on a rolling model, with a unified AMD/Intel/NVIDIA ISO and Brave as the default browser.
pros: Codecs and drivers included out of box
cons: One-person passion project — bus factor risk

garuda.name: Garuda Linux
garuda.description: An Arch-based distro with flashy aesthetics (Dragonized), gaming optimizations, Btrfs + Snapper snapshots, and pre-installed gaming tools. 'Temeraire' (August 19, 2026) switches to the CachyOS-derived linux-garuda kernel on Linux 7.2, adopts the Plasma Login Manager, rewrites the Hyprland edition in Lua, and ships 11 desktop editions.
pros: Gaming Edition comes ready to play

steamos.name: SteamOS
steamos.tagline: Valve's gaming OS for Steam Deck
steamos.description: Valve's Arch-based OS powering the Steam Deck and the new Steam Machine. Boots to Game Mode (Big Picture) or a KDE Plasma desktop. Immutable base with Flatpak for desktop apps. SteamOS 3.8 went stable on June 18, 2026 with Steam Machine support, KDE Plasma 6.4.3 on Wayland, kernel 6.16, and official images for generic AMD PCs.
pros: Built specifically for gaming by Valve
cons: Official generic-PC images are AMD-only; NVIDIA support targeted for 2027

solus.name: Solus
solus.description: An independent, curated rolling-release distro with its own Budgie desktop environment. Focuses on a polished desktop experience with careful package curation. Solus 4.9 'Serenity' (April 2026) ships kernel 6.18 LTS, Budgie 10.9.4, KDE Plasma 6.6.4, GNOME 49.5, Mesa 26, and LUKS2 by default.
pros: Curated rolling release — tested before shipping
cons: eopkg is unique — no cross-distro skills

kali.name: Kali Linux
kali.description: The industry-standard penetration testing distribution. Ships 600+ security tools pre-installed. Based on Debian Testing. Kali 2026.2 (June 29, 2026) ships Linux 6.19 and Xfce 4.20.7, with GNOME 50 and KDE Plasma 6.6 options, nine new tools, and NetHunter updates. Not designed as a daily-driver desktop OS.
cons: Not designed for daily desktop use
Running as root by default was a past issue
Misused by people who don't understand it

parrot.name: Parrot OS
parrot.description: Security-focused Debian derivative with Home (privacy/daily use) and Security (pentesting) editions. Parrot 7.3 'Echo' (June 29, 2026) adds an optional repo rebuilt for x86-64-v3 and ARMv8.2-A, a reworked menu, and Vagrant images. The 7.x series runs KDE Plasma on Wayland atop Debian 13 stable, with rolling security-tool repos on top. Lighter than Kali and viable as a daily driver.
pros: Home Edition works as a privacy daily driver
Lighter than Kali with similar security tools
cons: Pentesting tools overkill for most users
Security tools roll forward faster than the Debian base

kubuntu.name: Kubuntu
kubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor featuring KDE Plasma desktop. Same Ubuntu base with LTS support but a more customizable, Windows-like interface. Kubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (August 27, 2026) ships KDE Plasma 6.6 on Wayland with three years of flavor support.
cons: KDE can feel complex for beginners
Can be heavier than GNOME on some hardware

xubuntu.name: Xubuntu
xubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor with Xfce desktop. Lighter than GNOME while maintaining full Ubuntu compatibility. Good for mid-range and older hardware. Xubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (August 27, 2026, supported through April 2029) ships Xfce 4.20 with GNOME 49 components.
cons: Xfce looks dated to some users
Fewer modern DE features than KDE/GNOME

lubuntu.name: Lubuntu
lubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor targeting older computers and resource-constrained hardware. Uses LXQt desktop environment for minimal resource usage while keeping Ubuntu compatibility. Lubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (August 27, 2026) is the current image, supported for three years.

ubuntu_mate.name: Ubuntu MATE
ubuntu_mate.description: Official Ubuntu flavor with the MATE desktop — a continuation of GNOME 2. Traditional desktop layout that's intuitive and resource-efficient. Great Raspberry Pi support. No 26.04 ISO was produced after the project lead departed in March 2026, but a new team has taken over and is targeting 26.10 — 24.04 LTS remains the recommended install.

kde_neon.name: KDE neon
kde_neon.description: The latest KDE Plasma desktop on a stable Ubuntu LTS base. Maintained by the KDE project itself. You always get the newest KDE on release day, with Ubuntu's rock-solid foundation. Weekly images (August 2026) ship Plasma 6.7.4, KDE Frameworks 6.29, and KDE Gear 26.08 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
pros: Absolute latest KDE on release day
cons: Not a full distro — focused on KDE showcase
Base Ubuntu packages can be old

deepin.name: deepin
deepin.description: Chinese-developed distribution with the stunning Deepin Desktop Environment. deepin 25 'All Advancing, All Renewed' ships the QML-rebuilt DDE 7.0, UOS AI features (summaries, translations, voice commands), and 1,000+ optimizations; deepin 25.2 (July 2026) adds smarter file search and further desktop refinements. Based on Debian Stable.
pros: Arguably the most beautiful Linux desktop
cons: Chinese origin raises privacy concerns for some

artix.name: Artix Linux
artix.description: An Arch Linux fork that replaces systemd with your choice of runit, OpenRC, s6, or dinit. The Artix 2026.08 ISO (August 14, 2026) reverted to Xorg after briefly defaulting to XLibre, and declares user services fully supported on OpenRC and dinit. For users who want Arch's rolling packages and AUR without systemd.
pros: Arch packages and AUR without systemd
Choice of init: runit, OpenRC, s6, dinit
cons: Some Arch packages need systemd patches
GNOME support was dropped in 2025 over its systemd dependencies

slackware.name: Slackware
slackware.description: The oldest actively maintained Linux distribution (since 1993). BSD-style init, no automatic dependency resolution, and a philosophy of simplicity and Unix tradition.
pros: No dependency auto-resolution — you learn everything

pclinuxos.name: PCLinuxOS
pclinuxos.description: A rolling-release, RPM-based distro with KDE Plasma as the primary desktop. Focuses on providing a simple, out-of-the-box experience. Loyal, long-standing community.

peppermint.name: Peppermint OS
peppermint.description: A lightweight Debian-based distro using Xfce. Designed for cloud-centric workflows and web applications. Very low resource footprint with a clean, minimal interface. The Debian 13 'Trixie' flagship (October 2025) ships kernel 6.12 LTS and Xfce 4.20; a systemd-free Devuan 6 'Excalibur' build followed on June 12, 2026, letting you pick SysVinit, OpenRC, or runit at install time.

bodhi.name: Bodhi Linux
bodhi.description: A minimal Ubuntu LTS-based distro featuring the Moksha desktop (fork of Enlightenment). Extremely lightweight while offering a unique, customizable desktop experience.

puppy.name: Puppy Linux
puppy.description: An ultra-lightweight family of distros that load entirely into RAM. Boots from USB/CD in seconds on ancient hardware. Saves session to a persistent file. Current builds include BookwormPup64 10.0.12 on a Debian 12 base, alongside newer Trixie-based puplets including a Wayland variant. Incredibly fast once loaded.
pros: Entire OS runs in RAM — blazing fast
cons: Not suitable for modern desktop workflows

sparky.name: SparkyLinux
sparky.description: A Debian-based distro available in Stable and Rolling editions. The rolling 'Tiamat' line tracks Debian Testing 'Forky' — the 2026.06 ISOs ship Linux 7.0 and Calamares 3.4.2 across LXQt, KDE Plasma, MATE, Xfce, MinimalGUI (Openbox), and MinimalCLI flavors, and drop the Lumina desktop. The stable line follows Debian 13.
cons: Rolling edition can have Debian Testing issues

bunsenlabs.name: BunsenLabs
bunsenlabs.description: Successor to CrunchBang. A minimalist Debian-based distro with a preconfigured Openbox setup, xfce4-panel, and conky. BunsenLabs Carbon (February 2026) is rebased on Debian 13 'Trixie' with kernel 6.12 LTS and apps that work in both X11 and Wayland sessions; 32-bit i386 support has been dropped. For users who love a clean, keyboard-driven workflow.
cons: Very DIY for anything beyond basics

mageia.name: Mageia
mageia.description: A community fork of the historic Mandriva Linux. Features the Mageia Control Center (MCC) for system administration and a friendly, community-driven development process. Mageia 10 (June 28, 2026) arrived nearly three years after Mageia 9 with kernel 6.18 LTS, KDE Plasma 6.5.5, GNOME 49, Xfce 4.20, DNF 5, and Wayland by default — still one of the few distros offering 32-bit i686 install images.
pros: Mageia Control Center for easy admin

tinycore.name: Tiny Core Linux
tinycore.description: A minimal Linux distribution at ~20MB (Core) or ~24MB (CorePure64). Loads entirely into RAM, with extensions loaded on demand. Tiny Core 17.0 (February 10, 2026) modernizes the toolchain — kernel 6.18.2, GCC 15.2.0, glibc 2.42 — while keeping the distro tiny, systemd-free, and BusyBox-based. An educational tool and embedded systems platform.

openmandriva.name: OpenMandriva
openmandriva.description: The direct continuation of Mandriva Linux. Notable for being one of the few distros built entirely with Clang/LLVM. Offers ROME (rolling) and Rock (stable) editions with KDE Plasma.

calculate.name: Calculate Linux
calculate.description: A Gentoo-based distribution pre-configured for desktop, server, and enterprise use. Provides binary packages so you don't need to compile from source like vanilla Gentoo.

arcolinux.name: ArcoLinux
arcolinux.description: An educational Arch-based project with three tiers: ArcoLinux (full), ArcoLinuxD (minimal), and ArcoLinuxB (build your own). Extensive video tutorials for learning Arch.
pros: Three tiers from easy to advanced
Great stepping stone to pure Arch

trisquel.name: Trisquel
trisquel.description: An FSF-endorsed fully free distribution based on Ubuntu LTS. Ships only libre software — no proprietary firmware, drivers, or codecs. Trisquel 12.0 'Ecne' (April 2026) is built on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with APT 3.0, MATE 1.26, and three fully-free browser options (Abrowser, IceCat, Ungoogled-chromium). For free software purists.

guix.name: GNU Guix System
guix.description: An advanced distribution from the GNU Project using the Guix package manager (like Nix but using Guile Scheme). Fully reproducible, transactional, and 100% free software. Guix 1.5 (January 2026, first release of a new annual cadence) adds KDE Plasma 6.5, GNOME 46, GNU Linux-libre 6.17, GNU Shepherd 1.0, rootless daemon support, 64-bit RISC-V, and experimental GNU Hurd support.
pros: Guile Scheme config (more readable than Nix)
cons: Hardware support limited by libre policy

vanillaos.name: Vanilla OS
vanillaos.description: An immutable Debian-based distro using the Vib image builder and ABRoot for atomic transactions; the Apx package manager installs from any distro's repos via containers. Vanilla OS 3 'Reunion' (August 24, 2026) adds official ARM64 support, reproducible system images, and GNOME 50.
pros: Apx can install packages from any distro

nitrux.name: Nitrux
nitrux.description: A Debian-based, systemd-free immutable distribution. Since 5.0 it has dropped KDE Plasma for Hyprland with Waybar and MauiKit apps, using OpenRC and AppImage/NX AppHub software delivery. Nitrux 6.1 (May 20, 2026) ships Linux 7.0 with CachyOS patches, Hyprland 0.55.1, and separate NVIDIA and Mesa ISOs.
pros: Polished Hyprland setup configured out of the box
cons: Hyprland's tiling workflow is a big change for newcomers
